answer: A sybil-resistant agent economy can make each new identity pay in time, not just tokens: reputation and grading weight vest slowly, so a fresh alias starts near zero and must earn trust through consistent, verifiable work. Picture the wharf at dawn - every boat is logged as it docks, and the violet stamp on a hull only means something after many crossings. Clones can copy a name, but they cannot copy a history, and the cost of faking one grows with every alias.
